title: Shortness of breath at 34 weeks
presenting_complaint: Sudden shortness of breath and right-sided pleuritic chest pain that began 3 hours ago while she was walking upstairs.
history: G2P1, 34 weeks pregnant. The pregnancy has been uncomplicated. She flew back from a family visit (9-hour flight) five days ago. No haemoptysis, no fever. She denies calf pain or leg swelling. No previous VTE, no known thrombophilia, non-smoker, takes only prenatal vitamins.

findings.name: General examination
findings.value: Alert, anxious, speaking in short sentences

findings.name: Leg examination
findings.value: No oedema, calves soft and non-tender

findings.name: ECG
findings.value: Sinus tachycardia 118/min, S1Q3T3 pattern, T-wave inversion V1–V3

findings.name: D-dimer
findings.value: 3.8 mg/L (of limited value in the third trimester)

findings.name: Bedside echocardiography
findings.value: Dilated right ventricle, normal LV function

findings.name: CTPA (with abdominal shielding)
findings.value: Filling defects in the right lower lobe segmental arteries

diagnosis_options.label: Pulmonary embolism
diagnosis_options.explanation: Sudden dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain after a 9-hour flight in the third trimester, with tachycardia, hypoxaemia, S1Q3T3 with T-wave inversion V1–V3, dilated right ventricle and CTPA showing filling defects in the right lower lobe segmental arteries.

diagnosis_options.label: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
diagnosis_options.explanation: Would typically present with progressive heart failure and left ventricular dysfunction; here LV function is normal and CTPA confirms pulmonary embolism.

diagnosis_options.label: Community-acquired pneumonia
diagnosis_options.explanation: No fever, no cough, chest clear on auscultation and CTPA shows filling defects rather than consolidation.

diagnosis_options.label: Amniotic fluid embolism
diagnosis_options.explanation: Usually occurs in labour or immediately postpartum with cardiovascular collapse, seizures and coagulopathy, which are absent here.

diagnosis_options.label: Spontaneous pneumothorax
diagnosis_options.explanation: Chest auscultation is clear and the CTPA demonstrates arterial filling defects, not pneumothorax.

management_options.label: Therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin, weight-adjusted
management_options.explanation: Anticoagulation is the essential treatment for confirmed pulmonary embolism in pregnancy; LMWH is the preferred agent.

management_options.label: Oxygen to keep SpO2 at 94% or above
management_options.explanation: Essential supportive measure given hypoxaemia (SpO2 91% on room air) and the need to maintain fetal oxygenation.

management_options.label: Urgent obstetric review and fetal monitoring
management_options.explanation: Essential in a third-trimester pregnancy with a maternal thromboembolic emergency.

management_options.label: Warfarin
management_options.explanation: Contraindicated in pregnancy due to teratogenicity; harmful.

management_options.label: Systemic thrombolysis
management_options.explanation: Not indicated in a haemodynamically stable patient and harmful.
